headline: Nvidia's board is weighing whether to remove its CEO and the stock is down about 6% before the open, undoing part of Wednesday's CoreWeave rally; QQQ closed back over 683.69 but on light volume, so it is not a confirmed turn, and no put passes.
summary: Prices are Wednesday Nov 11 closes from Massive. The dashboard caught up at 13:55 UTC today (prices_as_of 2026-11-11), so verdicts and setups now use Nov 11 closes. Wednesday: CoreWeave rose 24.71% to 60.77 on 165.1 million shares, the S&P 500 gained 1.31% to 7,619.38 and the Nasdaq 1.60% to 25,466.19 (Massive; Motley Fool). QQQ closed 690.38, 0.98% over its 683.69 line, but on 44.9 million shares, below the 55 million we asked for, so it is a weak break. After the close the New York Times reported a second relationship by Nvidia's CEO and the Wall Street Journal said the board was preparing to remove him; no decision was announced by about 8:30am ET, NVDA was down about 6% before the open and Nasdaq 100 futures about 0.8% (Yahoo Finance; Reuters). Bonds reopen today with the 10 year at 4.99% and a $25 billion 30 year auction at 1pm ET. Nebius beat but guided low and raised capex, and Cisco, Applied Materials and Cerebras report after today's close. The put screen finds nothing: every strike is too thin.

signals.title: Nvidia's board weighs removing its CEO; the stock falls under its $164 floor before the open
signals.since_yesterday: The board met late Wednesday after the New York Times reported a second relationship, with an Nvidia executive; the Wall Street Journal said directors were preparing to remove the CEO and Bloomberg said an outside firm is looking for a successor. No decision had been announced by about 8:30am ET.
signals.what_happened: NVDA closed 173.73 on Nov 11, up 2.87%, on 339.2 million shares, before the news (Massive). After the close the New York Times reported the CEO had a second relationship, with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, and the Wall Street Journal reported the board was preparing to remove him. Bloomberg said Nvidia is working with an outside firm on a possible successor (Investing.com). NVDA traded about 7% lower at 160.85 before the bell (AP) and about 5.6% lower at 8:29am ET (Yahoo Finance), under a floor near $164 that held twice in 14 months (Yahoo Finance). AMD and AVGO rose before the open; CoreWeave, in which Nvidia owns about 13%, fell about 9% to 10% (AP; Yahoo Finance). No board statement was found as of this writing.
signals.so_what: This is now a leadership question, not just a probe. Second order: a CEO change days before the Nov 17 report means guidance and customer deals could be delayed or questioned, and customers already testing other chips may move faster, which is why AMD and AVGO rose. Third order: Nvidia funds or backs many AI buyers (CoreWeave, Anthropic's private placement), so doubts about Nvidia spread to its customers and to Anthropic's Nov 18 pricing. What would make this wrong: a quick, orderly handover with a strong interim leader and an unchanged outlook on Nov 17.
signals.for_you: No NVDA trade or put before Nov 17; the verdict is 'Wait'. AMD is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' (552.90 on Nov 11, zone 525.17 to 566.94); a bounce on Nvidia's trouble is not a chart signal. Keep any new AI swing small until Nov 19.

signals.title: Nebius beats but guides low and lifts capex; CoreWeave's 25% jump fades before the open
signals.what_happened: Nebius reported Q3 revenue of $980.8 million, up from $146.1 million a year ago and above the $907.5 million forecast (company release; CNBC). It expects 2026 revenue at the low end of $3.0 to $3.4 billion (FactSet expected $3.35 billion), raised 2026 capex to $27 billion from $20 to $25 billion, and plans $40 to $45 billion of 2027 capex against $12 to $13 billion of 2027 revenue (CNBC). Q3 capex was $7.3 billion and interest expense $112.5 million (release). NBIS closed 154.69 on Nov 11, up 15.44%, and fell about 10% before the open (Massive; CNBC). CoreWeave closed 60.77, up 24.71%, on 165.1 million shares, about 1.8 times Tuesday's volume, then fell about 9% to 10% before the open (Massive; Yahoo Finance; AP).
signals.so_what: Demand is real, but the neoclouds are spending several dollars of capex for each dollar of revenue, funded with debt and customer prepayments. Second order: that spending is revenue for Nvidia, power and cooling suppliers, as long as the funding holds. Third order: with yields near 5% and Nvidia's leadership in question, lenders and investors may ask for more, and the weakest neoclouds would feel it first. What would make this wrong: Cisco and Applied Materials guiding up tonight.
signals.for_you: NBIS is 'Watch' on the dashboard and closed far above its 91.00 to 136.49 zone; no trade. Do not chase CRWV after a 25% day and a 10% premarket drop. No puts.

signals.title: Anthropic IPO: reported several times oversubscribed, with a $26 billion placement to chip and cloud suppliers
signals.since_yesterday: Bloomberg reported the book is multiple times oversubscribed on large anchor orders (via MarketWatch), and the filings show a $26 billion private placement of Class N shares at the IPO price to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC (Quartz).
signals.what_happened: Anthropic is selling 825 million Class A shares at $70 to $78; with the placement it and its founders could raise up to $90.4 billion at the top of the range (Quartz, from filings). Pricing is planned for Nov 18 (Quartz). Yahoo Finance named it its company of the year on Nov 12 and reported revenue of more than $33 billion in the first nine months of 2026.
signals.so_what: Strong demand means the deal will likely price, but seven suppliers buying at the IPO price ties their books to how it trades. Second order: Nvidia's crisis lands the week before pricing, so a soft debut would hit the same chip names twice. Who wins is not clear until it prices, so no tickers are tagged.
signals.for_you: No action. Expect AI names to stay jumpy through Nov 19.

signals.title: China approves Lilly's weight loss pill first, ahead of Novo
signals.what_happened: China's NMPA approved orforglipron for adult weight management, the first oral GLP-1 for obesity approved in China; a type 2 diabetes filing is under review (Lilly China via PharmaPhorum, Nov 12). The FDA approved it on April 1, 2026 (Futu News). LLY rose about 2.8% before the open (Investing.com via Yahoo).
signals.so_what: A pill is cheaper to make and ship than an injection and needs no cold chain, which matters in a large cash pay market. Second order: it hurts Novo, whose oral semaglutide is approved in China for diabetes, not obesity. Third order: injectable device and fill finish suppliers (WST) lose a little of the long run story if pills take share. What would make this wrong: low pricing or slow hospital listing in China.
signals.for_you: Long term: LLY is 'Watch' with its price (1,437.29 on Nov 11) far above its 1,260 to 1,267 zone; no buy, no put.

signals.what_happened: The FCC accepted for filing SpaceX's application to buy 546 Grain Management 800 MHz licenses covering about 100% of the US population, about $8 billion. signals.for_you: Long term: TMUS is in its zone, but this is the risk to price in. Small first tranche only, and no TMUS put today (12 contracts traded). Watch Dec 1.
